purpose: Small, manually curated reference index to help visitors discover authoritative historical records, journal articles and books; no source content redistribution.
method: Human-reviewed extraction of factual titles, bylines, publication dates, resource types and subjects from institutional record pages, journal metadata/abstracts and publisher catalogues. No bulk scraping or full-text ingestion.

fieldDefinitions.authors: Named human writers or historical creator of the item, if directly verified; organization publisher is not inserted as author.
fieldDefinitions.contributors: Named contributors credited by the publisher, separate from authors.
fieldDefinitions.people: Named historical figures that an item discusses or that participate in the documented historical event. Writers appear here only if also substantive subjects or historical participants.
fieldDefinitions.places: Verified geographical locations mentioned in the source as relevant to its subject.
fieldDefinitions.communities: Verified specific community names or named communities/groups relevant to the resource.
fieldDefinitions.subjects: Researcher-assigned topical keyword tags supported by original titles, records, abstracts or publisher summaries.
fieldDefinitions.dates: Historical life/event/document dates with kinds, kept distinct from the modern publicationDate.
fieldDefinitions.publicationDate: Release date of article or book; does not represent the historical event.
fieldDefinitions.accessPoints: Original institutional landing pages; extra routes grouped in one record only if they point to the same named historical resource.

editorialSafety: Empty people/author/date fields mean not verified or not applicable, not missing inventable facts.
Journal descriptions are paraphrased from landing-page titles and abstracts, not from inaccessible full texts.
Book descriptions reflect public publisher catalogue information only; books were not read.
Copyrighted photographs, scans, article texts and books are not included.
Some Érudit record pages intermittently block automated visits; the official issue TOC, citations and abstracts support their entries.
Search-by-person should consult both people and authors fields without combining their meanings.
